Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the attachments. Quick answers up front and details below:

Summary (our preference)
- Preferred: Globex sends the full invoiced EUR amount and instructs your bank to set fees to OUR (sender pays fees). That ensures no netting and we reconcile gross revenue.
- If your bank cannot set OUR, we will accept net-of-fees, but Redwood requires the bank fee receipts for any fee reimbursement requests.
- VAT: Redwood US entity does not charge EU VAT. If Globex is VAT-registered and can reverse-charge, please include your VAT ID on the payment remittance. Otherwise your AP should treat as non-local supply; confirm with your tax team.

Routing details (to reduce intermediary fees)
- SEPA/EUR: Use our EUR clearing account (NL) with the reference: RWD-INV-4579. Include full IBAN on the wire template.
- If your bank insists on correspondent routing via Paris, please ask them to route via our primary clearing partner (Redwood partner bank) rather than using a third-party correspondent. If your bank needs a correspondent BIC, request they route to: PARTNER-BIC (ask your bank to confirm exact BIC in the wire UI).

When to involve finance: CCing Ben Carter (Finance) so he can track receipts and any fee-reimbursement follow-ups.

Action items for Globex:

- If not possible, send net and provide bank fee receipt(s) PDF with remittance.
- Add VAT ID in remittance if applicable.
- Use reference: RWD-INV-4579

Hi Elena — Ben from Finance here. Sorry for the delay, wanted to confirm policy and the easiest operational path.

Policy & operational guidance
- Preferred flow: Globex instructs your bank to set fees to OUR (sender pays). If your bank requires a correspondent BIC, ask them to route to our partner clearing bank and provide the partner BIC to you. This avoids third-party intermediary deductions in most cases.
- If your bank cannot do OUR and deducts the intermediary fee, Redwood will consider reimbursing small bank fees on a case-by-case basis, but we require: (a) the SWIFT fee stub or bank charge receipt, and (b) the original payment trace showing debit & credit amounts. Reimbursement is not automatic; it is reviewed.
- GBP to USD: We can accept GBP wires, but those will be converted on our end and may incur internal FX handling. That adds reconciliation overhead; please only use GBP-USD if the intermediary option cannot be avoided. Provide FX gross/net details when sending.

Practical next steps (to close this out quickly)
1) Please attempt a SEPA payment with reference RWD-INV-4579 and ask your bank to route to our partner clearing BIC. If they need the BIC text, tell them to contact our Treasury desk at treasury@redwood.com and we will confirm the exact correspondent information.
2) If they cannot set OUR, send the payment net and include the bank fee stub (PDF). Submit the stub to finance@redwood.com with the payment reference and we will evaluate reimbursement.
3) If you choose GBP->USD, state the FX rate and gross amount on the remittance so we can match application.

I realize this is annoying — happy to hop on a 15-minute call with your payments team to get the exact wire template working. If so, share a few windows in CET and I'll coordinate internally.
